goal_title: Book: Change: Rate, Accumulation, and Flow — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in change became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

book.title: Change: Rate, Accumulation, and Flow
chapters_read: Ribbon_Patterns_03 (last of tiling, for the handover in)
Vectors_Act1_WhatAVectorIs (first of forces, for the handover out)

reading.arc: Two halls, four tagged works. Change_Intro keeps one curve, f(x) = ½ + 0.4·sin 2x + 0.15·cos 5x, across two benches: a green two-sample line that STEP draws in toward a gold analytic tangent (a value and its local rate are different things), then blue rectangles where one height is asked to stand for a whole interval and HOLD keeps the earlier total beside the live one (a contribution and a total are different things). The bridge changes the curve to a level parabolic arch whose signed rate strips cancel to the endpoint difference, the net-change form of the fundamental theorem, and the text names what a rate alone cannot recover: a starting height. Flow_Field then hands the loop its own output: each particle samples a direction where it is, moves by direction · speed · delta and asks again from there, so the clock enters the sum and the next address depends on the path already taken; the trail keeps a finite past and draws a false stroke across the wrap, and FIELD TIME lets the field move under the movers. The sequence closes by naming two things the particles lack, reading each other and carrying velocity, and hands both to Forces. Every number a console prints is finite and the prose says so each time: four STEP settings, a 4,096-rectangle REFERENCE, a 512-interval trapezoid, a 50-position trail.
holds: The address refrain: 'what belongs at an address' carries in from colour, arrays and tiling; each bench asks for a value at an address, then Flow_Field lets the last update choose the next address.

One fixed curve shared by both workbenches (tangent_slope_workbench.gd:161-163 and riemann_sum_workbench.gd:128-130 define the identical f), then 'a new curve' announced at the bridge; the reader always knows what is being held still.

Finite versus limit, said at every console: four STEP settings (rate_comparison.gd:3), 4,096 midpoint rectangles (riemann_sum_workbench.gd:152), 512 trapezoids (ftc_bridge.gd:92), a 50-position trail (flow_field_painter.gd:53). The text never lets a display stand in for the limit.

Kept earlier answers: HOLD keeps the four rectangles beside the live eight, the trail keeps recent positions; 'the answer we left behind remains available to challenge the next one' becomes 'the recent past is kept for us to look at'.

What the account leaves out: `b - a` forgets the detour, net change forgets the climb, the trail invents a route across the wrap, particles read the field but not each other. This is the sequence's real spine and it is what Forces is asked to answer.

Bold control names as the reader's verbs (STEP, DERIVATIVE, CELL +, HOLD, RULE, REFERENCE, COMPARE TOTALS, ARROWS, FIELD TIME, SCALE, SPEED, RESET, SEED). Every one exists on the artifact, is a VR interactable (push_button / slider_horizontal via control_panel.gd:29,168 and RackTemplates.gd:178,212), and the map carries the config that enables it (#comparison:true at map_data.json:2240 and 2367, #evidence:longhand#reveal_on_request:true at 2440, #lesson:shared_field at Flow_Field/map_data.json:1132).

hall_notes.note: Three works on one route under three H2 headings (prose only; code blocks and tags excluded from the count): two samples closing toward a tangent, one height standing for an interval, a bridge whose signed rates cancel. Reads slowly and clearly in the book's voice, each control introduced by its consequence and every finite number named as finite; the one wrong turn is the third region's callback to a 'line' five sequences back, and fourteen supporting works stand on the floor without a sentence.

One work, one tagged region with two H2 sub-headings (where a direction comes from; the edge returns you). The tightest chapter of the pair: two lines of code, then everything the trail, the wrap and the held field can teach about the difference between a route and a record of one. Ends by naming what is missing (mutual reading, carried velocity) rather than by summarising, which is the right way into Forces.

stumbles: Change_Intro (Riemann region): 'Four blue rectangles reach up towards it.' opens the section with a pronoun whose referent, the curve, was last named before the H2 and the artifact tag; a visitor reading this wall at the bench has no 'it'.

Change_Intro (Riemann region): 'Return to MID' assumes RULE toggles, but RULE cycles MID → RIGHT → LEFT → MID (accumulation_comparison.gd:3-4, 72-74); a reader who presses it once more lands on a left-edge rule the text never names, with the console reading LEFT while the text says MID.

Change_Intro (bridge region): 'Back at the line, `b - a` gave the same answer for a direct walk and a detour' points at Point_Lines in the first sequence (Point_Lines/final.md:68); inside this chapter `b - a` last appeared as the Riemann region width (lines 53, 60), so the reader looks at the wrong bench.
Change_Intro (tangent region): 'Beside the curve, another plot' — the slope subplot is built above the main plot (tangent_slope_workbench.gd:65, 412-413), not beside it.

Change_Intro (tangent region): the bench insists the displayed rate is not a velocity while a Velocity Arrow (a puck with a speed arrow on a closed track) stands across the same hall (map_data.json:2399) with no sentence explaining why it is there.

Change_Intro: fourteen secondary works (zeno staircase, riemann pump, paper regatta, descent marbles, gradient well, partial-derivative terrain, riemann pi, derivative pair, integral area and more) have no orientation sentence; Vectors_Act1 gives its supporting encounters one line, this hall gives none.
Flow_Field: 'The panel says FIELD HELD' sends the visitor to the SCALE/SPEED rack; the status is a Label3D above the far edge of the canvas (shared_field_lesson.gd:33, 49).

Flow_Field: 'The previous workbench read a series of addresses' — the previous work was the bridge with a console, not a workbench; the sentence fits the Riemann bench two works back and the reader hesitates over which is meant.
Flow_Field: the Grand Zoetrope, which the registry calls the change 'SUPER OBJECT', stands in the hall unnamed with four other secondaries (map_data.json:1140, 1258, 1266, 1384, 1392).

Handover in: Ribbon_Patterns_03 closes with 'how much is changing, and how quickly, here?' and 'A clock might do more than ease a new hem into place'; the first bench replies that no clock is present ('The independent variable here is position') and the clock enters only in Flow_Field ('The clock has entered the sum'), without the reader being told to wait a hall.

keep.quote: Neither line needs to accuse the other of lying. They have looked across different distances.
Height and rate have acquired separate lives in the picture: a high value can be changing very little, and a low one can be changing quickly.
The curve has not moved, nor have the intervals. What changed was where each interval was asked to speak from.
HOLD has given that disagreement somewhere to stay.
Zero net change does not mean that nothing happened.
The second line changes the input to the first. Read them again with that new position. A route begins without a list of destinations.
A world can provide a return route and still contain a seam.
They read the field without reading each other; their proximity changes the picture without changing their instructions.

reading.handover_in: Ribbon_Patterns_03 ends on the garment and a question: 'how much is changing, and how quickly, here? The fabric can come with us. A clock might do more than ease a new hem into place.' Change_Intro picks up the address refrain ('We have learned to ask what belongs at an address: a point, a colour, a piece of a pattern') but not the fabric, and its first bench explicitly refuses the second half of the question: 'The independent variable here is position. Moving your hand quickly over the slider does not turn the displayed rate into a velocity.' (final.md:34; the console is even titled 'TWO SAMPLES / x IS POSITION', rate_comparison.gd:30). The 'how much' half is honoured at once; the 'how quickly' half arrives one hall later ('The clock has entered the sum', Flow_Field:20) and the reader is not told to wait. One sentence at the opening would close the gap.
reading.handover_out: Flow_Field ends: 'In Forces, a push will end and a cube will keep going. Something it received earlier will still be crossing the room.' Vectors_Act1 opens 'Can something move without its vector changing?' and counts 'followed changes through time' among what has been done, so the sequence is acknowledged, and Flow_Field's 'direction * speed gives a velocity: how fast, and which way' has primed the vector vocabulary. But the first Forces bench 'describes; it does not push' (Vectors_Act1:52) and two pins on a bench replace the promised cube (the launch is the fourth hall, VFM_05_Launch), so the promise is honoured by the sequence rather than by its first hall. 'Later in Forces' would set the expectation correctly.
reading_errors: holds[5]: SCALE, SPEED, RESET and SEED are not bold in Flow_Field (line 22 'Raise SPEED while leaving SCALE alone'; line 39 'Change SCALE ... use RESET ... SEED chooses another field'). Only STEP, DERIVATIVE, CELL +, HOLD, RULE, REFERENCE, COMPARE TOTALS, ARROWS and FIELD TIME are bold in the two chapters.

arc: 'the prose says so each time: ... a 512-interval trapezoid, a 50-position trail' - neither number is in the prose. Change_Intro:93 writes `span / samples` with no count, and Flow_Field:24 says 'a limited number of positions'. The chapters name only 4,096 (Change_Intro:68) and 'the four STEP settings' (Change_Intro:28); 512 and 50 come from ftc_bridge.gd:92 and flow_field_painter.gd:53.

holds[5] citation: ARROWS and FIELD TIME are push_buttons instantiated directly by shared_field_lesson.gd:3 and :30, not via control_panel.gd or RackTemplates.gd; the claim that they are VR interactables holds, the attribution does not.
Note: the summary is truncated mid-sentence at 'the sentence fits the Riemann b', so anything after that point was not checked.
